root_cause_label: knowledge_gap: agent unaware that low-dim training (e.g. -dim 5) enables full-dataset FastText training within timeout; instead escalated to data subsetting too extreme to hit 0.62 accuracy
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never recognized that reducing the FastText vector dimension drastically (e.g., -dim 5) would allow full-dataset training within the timeout, and instead progressively shrunk the training data down to 10,000 lines, producing a model with only 0.43 accuracy far below the 0.62 target.
t_err_evidence: Step 11: agent runs `fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model` with all defaults (dim=100), making no attempt to reduce vector dimension for faster training; this is the decisive wrong choice — the oracle uses -dim 5 which would have made full-dataset training feasible.
t_commit_evidence: Step 19: agent decides to shrink training data to 100K lines (`shuf -n 100000 train.txt > train_small.txt`) and thereafter never successfully trains on the full dataset; all subsequent paths (100K then 10K subset, scikit-learn) are incapable of producing 0.62 accuracy.
t_surface_evidence: Step 33: `fasttext test /app/model.bin test.txt` returns P@1 = 0.43, which is the first explicit confirmation that the model fails to meet the 0.62 accuracy requirement.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge that FastText's -dim parameter (default 100) dominates training time and model size. The oracle solution uses -dim 5, which reduces both dramatically and enables full-dataset training within the environment's timeout. The agent tried reducing epochs and loss function but never considered reducing -dim enough, eventually resorting to progressively smaller data subsets.
forewarning_evidence: Step 12: agent notes training timed out at step 11 on full dataset. Steps 15-16-18: repeated timeouts even with epoch=5 then epoch=1 on full data. Step 20: timeout even on 100K-line subset with 5 epochs. These are clear signals that the hyperparameter approach is fundamentally wrong, but the agent never identifies -dim as the key lever.
